topics.label: Introduction to cancer biology and lecture learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes students to the lecture series and sets out its learning outcomes and framing.

topics.label: Genetic and epigenetic changes in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the kinds of changes that accumulate as cells progress toward malignancy and the questions that raises.

topics.label: Cancer as a failure of differentiation and tissue architecture
topics.groupedBecause: These ideas explain cancer as a breakdown in cellular differentiation and the orderly organization of tissues.

topics.label: Cell culture models of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic considers what cancer cells grown in culture can reveal and what those models leave out.

topics.label: Invasion and metastatic progression in tumors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how invasive growth distinguishes malignant tumors, how it is assessed, and how it can lead to metastasis.

topics.label: Malignant potential and harmful effects of benign tumors
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains that benign tumors may progress to malignancy or cause serious harm without doing so.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic sets out the naming conventions used to distinguish tumor types and their malignancy.

topics.label: How tumors cause illness and death
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how tumors disrupt normal function and how advanced disease can lead to death.

topics.label: Tumor incidence in humans and other animals
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics compare how often tumors occur across human populations and other animal groups.

topics.label: Cancer screening: rationale, methods, and limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain why screening is used and how its methods and limitations vary across cancer types.

topics.label: Lecture close and revision guidance
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture and points students toward revision, discussion, and upcoming practicals.
